gaps.lead: She cooked a huge meal, but we had already eaten.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it happened although it wasn't necessary.

gaps.lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
gaps.explanation: should(n't) have + participle criticises a past decision.

gaps.lead: The committee probably won't change the rules.
gaps.sentence: ___ the committee will change the rules.
gaps.explanation: probably won't = it is (highly) unlikely that.

gaps.lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.

gaps.lead: He enjoys his work despite his low salary.
gaps.explanation: 'though' can close a sentence as a soft 'however'.

gaps.lead: We couldn't see the lighthouse anywhere.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'nowhere' forces inversion: Nowhere could we see…
